messages:
maya: heads up — bringing up hf://s-embed-bert-v2 in private. conversion finished but embedding outputs differ from HF baseline.
liam: difference how big? cosine drift or token-level mismatch?
sasha: often these are tokenizer issues — special tokens or truncation strategy. can you paste the HF config you converted?
maya: pasted below. run was `redwood convert --source hf/s-embed-bert-v2 --mode embed --out ./redwood-config.json`

```
{
  "tokenizer": "bert-base-uncased",
  "do_lower_case": true,
  "special_tokens_map": {"cls_token": "[CLS]", "sep_token": "[SEP]"},
  "pooling": {"method": "cls", "cls_use_pooler": false},
  "truncation": {"strategy": "longest_first", "max_length": 512}
}
```

natalie: two quick suspects: (1) our conversion layer is inserting a leading space or adding `cls` token twice, (2) our embed runtime uses `cls` pooling but then applies `right` truncation which shifts tokens.
liam: can you run a tokenization diff for the same input on HF vs Redwood runtime? quick snippet:

```
input = "Review: model changed tokenization on short docs"
hf_tokens = hf_tok.encode(input)
red_tokens = red_tok.encode(input)
print(hf_tokens)
print(red_tokens)
```

maya: ran it. HF: [101, 7592, 1010, 2947, ... , 102]
maya: Redwood: [101, 7592, 1010, 2947, 102]
maya: note HF had padding/subword residuals; ours dropped a trailing 0? output lengths not matching for longer texts.
sasha: that looks like truncation side-effect. which truncation param did convert set? `longest_first` vs `only_first` matters for chat templates.

convert-bot: conversion log: detected tokenizer=bpe, detected special_tokens={'cls_token':'[CLS]'}, mapped to redwood_tokenizer with add_prefix_space=false

natalie: add_prefix_space=false is suspicious — sentencepiece/bpe models often need add_prefix_space=true or you get different merges.
liam: also pooling: HF `cls` pooling often expects the model to output CLS as first token; some sentence-transformers use mean pooling. were you sure the HF config used CLS?
maya: original readme said `pooling: cls` but training used mean pooling at fine-tune. hmm.
sasha: easiest check: compute embeddings with and without explicit `[CLS]` token and compare distances. also try switching truncation to `only_first` and keep max_len=256 to match eval harness.
maya: running three quick experiments now: (A) set add_prefix_space=true, (B) switch pooling->mean, (C) truncation->only_first. will post results.

liam: small note — if you change pooling to mean, you must ensure kv-cache/streaming paths don't apply CLS shortcuts. also watch for quantized kernels that do int8 rounding causing tiny drift.

maya: results:
- A (add_prefix_space=true): token sequences now match HF for most inputs, cosine similarity median -> 0.997
- B (mean pooling): qualitative eval on bertscore/bench: small improvement on sentence-sim but change in ranking for ~2% of pairs
- C (only_first, max_len=256): prevents midsentence truncation observed in customers' docs; similarity median -> 0.995 but fewer catastrophic drops

natalie: great. I suggest we: (1) update conversion to detect bpe/sentencepiece and set add_prefix_space accordingly, (2) add a heuristic to prefer `mean` pooling for models in the sentence-transformers family unless `cls_use_pooler=true` explicitly in HF config, (3) default truncation to only_first for emb/rerank workloads with max_len=512 fallback.
sasha: agree. open a PR? include a small test that tokenizes 10 randomized docs and asserts exact token sequences vs HF when mapping rules apply.

maya: opened PR #2147 with tests + conversion patch. pinging @liam for review.
liam: reviewing shortly. can we add a short note in model catalog that conversion may change pooling semantics and we log the inferred settings in model metadata? want customers to be able to audit.
atalie: yep — metadata should include `inferred_tokenizer_flags` and `inferred_pooling`. add to the console model detail page.

sasha: one more gotcha — chat templates: if a model uses chat-format and you convert it for embed-only, ensure system messages aren't prepended when computing embeddings; else you get biased vectors.
maya: confirmed. thanks all. follow-ups: PR + catalog metadata + add a fail-open flag to use raw HF tokenizer if conversion uncertain.
liam: :thumbsup:
convert-bot: deployment scheduled to staging in 10m — conversion tests will run automatically.
